title: Professional Life
text:
Work History
My first professional position was with WIL Research, LLC in Ashland, Ohio; where I joined the Developmental and Reproductive Toxicology department as a Biologist. My work focused on non-clinical toxicology and teratology assessment of new food/drug products using animal models. I recorded behavioral/physical changes in mothers and their offspring after a course of test compound treatment. These results helped inform sponsor and regulatory body decisions regarding administration of the compound to expectant mothers and newborns.
After several years of working at WIL, I began working for David Katz of the CWRU Neurosciences department. Our work focused on a mouse model of Rett Syndrome, a very rare X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder affecting females (primarily, it’s rare and usually lethal in males), in which normal development ceases shortly after birth and patients regress into severe Autism-like symptoms. My work was focused primarily on behavior outcomes using a genetic mouse model of this disease. We saw promising improvements in behavior (primarily in respiration disturbances, a very severe phenotype in the human Rett population as well as our model). I worked in the Katz lab for 10 years, eventually serving as Lab Manager/Research Assistant 4 where I handled administrative duties and served as the lead researcher for several large projects.
My current position is with the CWRU Core Research Facilities, as the manager for the Mouse Behavioral Phenotyping Core. My duties include consulting and training labs in the performance and interpretation of mouse behavior experiments, ensuring compliance with institutional standards and oversight, and other equipment maintenance and behavior testing as needed.

title: About Me
text: I enjoy spending time with my wife and two children (15 and 13 years old). We usually pursue outdoor activities and our favorite vacation spots include mountains or the beach. I volunteer with my son’s Boy Scout Troop as an Assistant Scout Master. We’ve gone on camping adventures in 5 different states and are planning a trip to the Florida Keys in June. I also volunteer with my local Kiwanis Club, which I joined in 2020. Our club focuses on providing services and funds to youth organizations in our area. When I have free time I enjoy fishing (especially with my kids), skiing, golfing and gardening.
